mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10Y-2Y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in the unemployment rate below 4% signals a labor market so tight that wage inflation will soon accelerate, prompting the Fed to raise rates and depress equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Core PCE inflation remains below 2% for the subsequent 6 months, indicating that wage pressures are not spilling over into broad price inflation.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production growth slows sharply (3-month change < -2%), it signals a supply chain disruption that will negatively impact corporate earnings and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 earnings estimates are revised upward by > 2% during the signal period, indicating that the supply shock is not materially impacting profits.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 4%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that will slow economic growth and depress equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Real GDP growth accelerates in the subsequent two quarters, indicating that the economy is resilient to higher rates.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts growth accelerates (3-month change > 10%), it signals a strengthening housing market that will boost consumer spending and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 30-year mortgage rates rise by > 50 basis points in the subsequent month, indicating that housing affordability is being eroded.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment growth slows sharply (3-month change < 100k), it signals a weakening labor market that will depress consumer spending and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Initial jobless claims fall by > 10% in the subsequent month, indicating that the labor market is rebounding.

mechanism_narrative: When real retail sales growth accelerates (3-month change > 5%), it signals a strengthening consumer sector that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer confidence index falls by > 10 points in the subsequent month, indicating that the spending impulse is fading.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI inflation rate rises above 3%, and the federal funds rate is below 2%, it signals a dangerous mix of high inflation and loose monetary policy that will lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The Fed raises rates by > 50 basis points at the next FOMC meeting, indicating that they are serious about combating inflation.
